medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The student body and faculty represent a variety of backgrounds and experiences. The school is actively involved in outreach, engagement, and retention of students from various backgrounds and communities.  Students from underrepresented populations who have the potential and are interested in pursuing an M.D. degree are encouraged to learn more about the 'Imi Ho'ola Post-Baccalaureate Program.  For more information, contact Dr. Winona Lee, Imi Ho'ola Post-Baccalaureate Program Director (winonal@hawaii.edu, ph. 808 692 1035).
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: To be used for any period of absence up to one year. Written requests require the approval of the Directors of Medical Education and Student Affairs for administrative leave. If a student is requesting a leave of absence because of academic difficulties (academic leave), s/he must appear before the Student Standing and Promotion prior to any approval. All student leaves are monitored by the Office of Student Affairs.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Students are engaged in a number of organizations and events that include Alpha Omega Alpha, student government, Interclass Council, specialty area interest groups, the Student Wellness Interest Group, the student-run HOME project for the houseless, the Willed Body Program, the Med Student Mentorship Program, the intramural basketball league, AMSA, community health fairs, and the annual JABSOM lu'au.  Additionally, students participate in interest groups related to specialties, community specific engagement and service, and research.  Co-curricular activities also include a variety of opportunities to learn about our host population and the culture of Hawai'i.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The John A. Burns School of Medicine is located on a 10.5-acre state-owned parcel in Kaka'ako on the water's edge between Waikiki and downtown Honolulu. During a student's tenure in the MD Program at the School of Medicine, there are opportunities to study on the various islands of Hawaii as well as throughout Asia and the Pacific Basin.  The School of Medicine is also an environment conducive to one of the school's goals:  becoming a top-ranked research-intensive medical school with the opportunity to attract world-class research scientists to join the school's faculty.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Medical students and candidates for graduate degrees are expected to make their own living arrangements. The University of Hawai'i at Manoa campus provides limited dormitory and apartment facilities.

medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The seventh graduation objective at JABSOM relates to "Wellness and Resiliency"  whereby "Graduates will have the skills and strategies to maintain wellness and resiliency."  Please refer to our website:  https://osa.jabsom.hawaii.edu/student-wellness/ for further information regarding wellness at JABSOM.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
The students, faculty and staff of the John A. Burns School of Medicine share a commitment to excellence and leadership in:  Educating current and future healthcare professionals and leaders; Delivering high-quality healthcare; Conducting research and translating discoveries into practice; Establishing community partnerships and fostering multidisciplinary collaboration; Pursuing alliances unique to Hawaiʻi and the Asia-Pacific region; Acting with forethought regarding right relationships, respect, and moral action.
The school aims to be the premier medical school in the Pacific - training and educating a  community of physicians, biomedical scientists and allied health workers who are committed to a vision of Attaining Lasting Optimal Health for All.
We are excited and look forward to welcoming those with this same intention to our unique training program and the JABSOM ʻOhana.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: JABSOM provides general guidelines for appropriate appearance and attire.  Special guidelines exist for students in clinical settings, laboratory and operating room experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Faculty office hours and additional tutoring are available.  JABSOM also has a clinical psychologist who is available for group and one-on-one sessions.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students at JABSOM begin patient interaction in their first year of medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: The curriculum utilizes a problem-based learning (PBL) format.  Other teaching methods used in complementary activities include but are not limited to small group teaching, lectures, and colloquia.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Students at JABSOM begin their clinical exposure in the first year via a clinical mentoring program.  Formal Clinical Rotations commence in the third year with placement at sites throughout the State.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance at lectures in the pre-clinical years is optional.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The school's problem-based learning curriculum (PBL) is an integrated approach to  basic  and clinical sciences using health care problems supplemented by lecture and laboratory sessions. Clinical skills and community health activities begin in the first year. Special features include the use of PBL in the pre-clinical years; early introduction of clinical training, community service, and research experiences; rural health opportunities throughout the State of Hawaii including the Kauai Medical Training Track; a longitudinal, interdisciplinary clerkship in the third-year; and opportunities for training experiences in various communities throughout Hawaii, the Pacific, and Asia.  Students each have a longitudinal clinical mentor and are placed into Learning Communities that provide further mentorship and teaching as well as continuity in the areas of professionalism, patient safety, clinical skills, ethics, community- and social-responsiveness, health systems science, and wellness and resiliency.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Students are introduced to primary care in the first year of medical school through clinical experiences, PBL case studies, community health course sites, and lectures/panels.  Required third-year clinical rotations include family medicine, pediatrics, and internal medicine.  Rural health opportunities and student interest groups are available throughout the curriculum.

medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Students rotate through a variety of affiliated community hospitals and clinics that reflect the breadth of our communities in the State of Hawaii.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The University of Hawai'i at Manoa John A. Burns School of Medicine  (JABSOM) is in the College of Health Sciences and Social Welfare. JABSOM is located in Kaka'ako with teaching facilities in affiliated community hospitals and primary care clinics throughout the state.  JABSOM strives to improve the quality, effectiveness, and equity of health care delivery in Hawai‘i and the Pacific region. The school provides opportunity for qualified applicants including students from various underrepresented socioeconomic and minority groups to qualify for an MD degree; provides MD graduates with competency to enter postgraduate programs; and provides residency training programs with emphasis on primary-care specialties.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
JABSOM, as part of the fabric of Hawai‘i, is a diverse learning community
committed to excellence and leadership in:
- Educating current and future healthcare professionals and leaders
- Delivering high-quality healthcare
- Conducting research and translating discoveries into practice
- Establishing community partnerships and fostering multidisciplinary collaboration
- Pursuing alliances unique to Hawaiʻi and the Asia-Pacific region
- Acting with forethought regarding right relationships, respect, and moral action. 

Each JABSOM student is placed into a Learning Community that provides longitudinal mentorship, support and education as they progress through our curriculum.  Curricular and co-curricular activities echo the school's mission statement and students participate in a variety of educational programs the support our communities including those across the State of Hawai'i and the Pacific Basin.  Students who are interested in rural health may opt to participate in our Rural Health Track.  Global Health experiences are offered to allow students the opportunity to learn in Asia and the Pacific Basin.

Our graduates pursue a variety of specialties and many choose primary care specialties.  More than half of all physicians practicing in Hawai'i have trained at JABSOM as a medical student, resident or fellow.

Members of our JABSOM community engage in outreach efforts to encourage, mentor  and provide opportunities to students interested in pursuing careers in healthcare.  These outreach efforts emphasize the JABSOM mission.  The JABSOM admissions committee members and interviewers participate in annual training workshops that focus on the selection of applicants who are mission-aligned and who are committed to improving the healthcare of our communities.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: The minimum requirement is two individual letters of evaluation or you may submit your school Pre-Medical/Pre-Health Committee letter or packet.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: It is highly suggested that letters be written by individuals who know the applicant well; have spent a significant time with them; and who are able to speak to the applicant's work and/or abilities and capabilities.  Letter writers should be able to provide an impartial assessment of the applicant.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Invitations to interview may be sent as early as August 1.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews will be conducted online.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: A secondary application will be sent to applicants who submit a complete AMCAS application and pay the $150 secondary application fee.

medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: MCAT scores are but one part of the application considered for admission to JABSOM.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: JABSOM does not have a minimum GPA to be considered for admission.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: An applicant must complete 90 college level semester credit hours (or 135 quarter hours) from a regionally accredited U.S. institution or a similarly accredited institution in Canada to be considered for admission to JABSOM.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Community college coursework from an accredited US or Canadian school may be used to meet JABSOM’s prerequisite requirements.  Review is required.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants may submit letters describing significant updates or achievements .

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Financial status is not a factor in considering applicants for acceptance. Efforts are made to assist medical students in obtaining loans and scholarships wherever possible. Loan funds from federal sources are available only to U.S. citizens and permanent residents. In general, students are discouraged from engaging in outside employment.  Applicants are referred to the Scholarship Director/Financial Literacy Counselor, Office of Student Affairs at the John A. Burns School of Medicine or to the University of Hawaii at Manoa Financial Aid Services Office for further information.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: All tuition and fee charges at the UH campuses are subject to change in accordance with requirements of state law and action by the Board of Regents or the UH administration. We, at the John A. Burns School of Medicine, realize the significant costs involved in a medical education.  Our Scholarship Director/Financial Literacy Counselor is prepared to discuss with students their options regarding scholarships and other resources.  Students are encouraged to make an appointment for further information and assistance.

medSchoolAssessments.assessmentAdditionalInformation: AAMC PREview® Exam Required - To be considered for admission to JABSOM, an applicant is required to submit a AAMC PREview® Exam score taken within three years prior to matriculation.You must submit a PREview score for your application to be considered complete.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: The JABSOM waitlist shall remain open from the date that decision letter are sent until the first day of school.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Information about the required/recommended premedical coursework and competencies for JABSOM admission may be found on the JABSOM website.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: JABSOM does not have an expiration policy regarding prerequisite courses, although it is highly recommended that students take refresher courses when needed to be prepared for entry to medical school.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Applicants are considered without discrimination as to age, sex, race, color, national or ethnic origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, creed, religion, veteran status or marital status. The school admits 77 students to its first-year class. Though not a requirement,  it is desirable that an applicant has some sort of tie to the State of Hawai'i. Application screening is  a two-tiered process. The first determines an applicant's ties to the State of Hawai'i.  The second requires both ‘resident’ and ‘nonresident’ applicants to meet a minimum cut-off score to proceed through the admissions process. Applicants who pass the second screen are considered for interviews.  Applicants are responsible for scheduling three one-on-one interviews which will be conducted virtually for the 2026 application season.  One of the three interviews is with the Director of Admissions.  Acceptance, waitlist, and regret letters are emailed in  mid-March.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: We strongly recommend that applicants confirm their interest and suitability for a career in medicine. Shadowing is one means of doing this; however, it is not the only accepted method. For example, applicants may wish to explore alternate clinical opportunities such as volunteer service or employment in a clinical setting to gain similar enriching experiences.
